newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The feelings of concern prevailing in recent weeks over the rate of returns in tax revenues were confirmed at yesterday's meeting on the course of the economy, chaired by Prime Minister Costas Simitis. However, the government's economic team has decided not to take any additional measures to boost inflows until the end of May.

--The Elefsina Shipyards will be transferred within the month to a company established by the Neorion shipyards, an inter-ministerial committee on privatisation decided yesterday. Cabinet is expected to give its approval to the move.

--The government's proposals on changes to the job market will be based on an experts' report examined yesterday at a ruling party PASOK meeting. The report recommends the full deregulation of the labour market (abolishing restrictions on sackings and compensation) and reduction of wage levels.
--Reliable sources say collective wage agreements with employees at public utilities and organisations (DEKOs) have settled on 10.5 wage increases for the 1997-1998 period

--Fears of the political cost have led to a veil of secrecy being drawn over initial proposals on social dialogue between unions, government and employers at yesterday's joint ruling party-government meeting.
--Excessive fluidity is expected to lead to rate cuts in the interbank market.

--Simitis revealed his 19-point proposal for social dialogue at yesterday's meeting and insisted on the need to create a "climate of flexibility" in the job market, including proposals for part-time work in the public sector and local work agreements.
--Greece is likely to be left out in the cold if it does not soon make moves to link up with two major energy networks in Europe - the Norway-Italy and North African-Italy natural gas networks.
--Thirty new economic crimes squad teams yesterday conducted surprise checks and audits on more than 300 firms, on the first day of the squad's operation.
--The next two months are critical for the public finances: if the disappointing returns to date do not change in this period then corrective measures are considered to be a certainty.
--The need to make further investments to keep abreast of developments will lead Greek informatics firms to increase share capital.

--Greece will have company: a recent European Union report says that Germany and Italy will join Greece on the sidelines in the final phase of Economic and Monetary Union as their public deficits in 1997 will above the 3.0 percent of GDP level.
